bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price risk - exposure to plastic resin and agricultural commodity prices with no effective hedge — The Company's businesses remain exposed to fluctuations in prices of key raw materials, particularly plastic resins and certain agricultural commodities. Since effective hedging mechanisms for plastic resins are not available, it can only monitor market movements and adjust procurement, pricing and inventory strategies; PVC resin swings during FY2026 drove channel inventory rationalisation and cautious dealer procurement.
- Liquidity and working-capital risk — Liquidity management is explicitly listed among corporate-level risks. The Company relies on a disciplined approach to operating cash flow and working capital efficiency - retail-led model, cash-and-carry sales, improved collections, inventory optimisation and prudent capital allocation - and reports that it continued to meet all debt servicing obligations and maintained its borrowings as 'Standard' with all lending institutions.
- Receivables and collection risk, especially under Government-supported programmes — Timely recovery of receivables, particularly under Government-supported programmes, remains an important focus area. Mitigation is a deliberate shift towards the retail-led business model and cash-and-carry sales while reducing dependence on project-based business, backed by dealer relationships and disciplined credit management.
- Climate change and weather risk — Changing climatic conditions, erratic rainfall patterns, extreme weather events and increasing pressure on water resources continue to impact agricultural activity and demand across the Company's businesses - the same forces that also create demand for its climate-smart irrigation and water-management solutions.
- Demand risk tied to agricultural activity, Government policy and infrastructure spending — Demand across businesses is influenced by agricultural activity, Government policies, infrastructure spending, rural income levels and overall economic conditions, making the order profile dependent on programme implementation; the Company leans on its MIS, extensive dealer network and market intelligence to track requirements.
- Geopolitical and global economic risk — Geopolitical developments, changing international trade policies, reciprocal tariff measures, supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures and global economic uncertainty may impact both domestic and international operations; diversification and global presence are the stated mitigants.
- Interest rate and foreign exchange risk — Domestic and international operations expose the Company to interest rate and currency movements; it uses treasury management practices including forward exchange contracts where considered necessary, alongside a continued focus on cash flows and working capital.
- Capacity utilisation risk — Utilisation across businesses may be influenced by seasonal demand, Government programme implementation, customer demand patterns and overall market conditions; the Company works to improve it through product diversification, retail expansion, export growth, value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations.
- Agri-input supply and crop-cycle risk in Agro-Food Processing — The food business faces unpredictable weather, changing crop patterns, inflationary pressures, agricultural commodity price fluctuations, rising logistics and supply chain costs, and availability of quality agricultural produce; mitigation runs through the integrated farm-to-fork model, contract farming and a diversified sourcing network.

business.body: JISL operates across three business verticals: Hi-Tech Agriculture Solutions (micro and sprinkler irrigation systems, tissue culture, planting material and solar agri pumps), Plastic Piping Systems (PVC and PE pipes for agriculture, infrastructure and plumbing applications) and Agro Processing (through its subsidiary Jain Farm Fresh Foods Limited and overseas subsidiaries in the UK, USA, Belgium and Turkey). outlook.body:
- Grow the retail and cash-and-carry businesses, widen the dealer network and deepen presence across Northern, Eastern and North-Eastern India
- Expand exports and value-added businesses while continuing to improve collections and working-capital efficiency
- Make significant repayments of long-term debt in FY2027 to strengthen the balance sheet further; focus on free cash generation, collections, prudent investment and profitable growth while finance costs remain high
- Invest in climate-smart irrigation, biotechnology, disease-resilient planting material, protected cultivation, digital farming, solar energy, food technology and circular agricultural systems - extending leadership into areas where research, brands, infrastructure and farmer relationships give a clear advantage
- Move research from the laboratory to commercial cultivation: commercialised coffee and black pepper tissue culture and strengthened tissue-culture banana against Fusarium Wilt using bio-immunisation technology licensed from ICAR, Lucknow
- Build out industrial-scale biochar capacity converting agricultural and fruit-processing residue into carbon-rich soil input, creating potential for farmers to participate in the emerging carbon economy - the Jalgaon unit is the first of several units planned
- Develop private-label and co-manufacturing platforms in Agro Processing, building on strengths in fruit sourcing, processing, food safety and customer relationships
- Extend piping capability beyond manufacturing into execution of technically complex water infrastructure, strengthening position in subsea intake and outfall systems
- Maintain an integrated farm-to-fork model in food - contract farming, varietal development, traceability and long farmer relationships - with international operations in the UK, USA, Belgium and Turkey keeping the business close to global customers
- Strengthen market position in plastics through product innovation, value-added portfolio expansion, wider distribution reach, cost optimisation and operational efficiency
- Aspire to be more agile and focused, using decades-old businesses and relationships to endure difficult cycles and steady investment in new technologies, crops, applications and markets to evolve
- The Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to the SEBI notification dated 8th July, 2016, which is published on its website along with its Nomination and Remuneration Policy, Disclosure of Information Policy, Centralised Purchase Policy, Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy and other governance documents; the routed governance sections state the policy framework rather than a payout ratio or reinvestment target. Governance philosophy is centred on enhancing stakeholder value with equal consideration to all stakeholders, with integrity, product quality and transparency as core values, and where the Companies Act, 2013 and the SEBI Listing Regulations differ the Company follows the more stringent requirement. The Company reports that it did not have any material related party transactions during the year and discloses arm's length transactions that are either pre-approved (such as long-term lease arrangements), recurring transactions with subsidiaries, or CSR activities approved by the Board and CSR Committee. The Company has not issued any convertible securities or granted stock options to any of its Non-Executive Directors.
- BRSR 2025-26 disclosures were independently assured by TÜV India Private Limited (TUVI) under ISAE 3000 (Revised) - reasonable assurance over the applicable BRSR Core disclosures and the nine BRSR principles, with limited assurance over Essential and Leadership Indicators and GRI Standards 2021 disclosures
- Assurance boundary is limited to 11 manufacturing facilities and excludes corporate offices, sales offices, overseas subsidiaries, joint ventures and associate entities, so reported KPIs may not represent the entirety of JISL's global operations
- Facilities inside the BRSR verification boundary: JISL Plastic Park, Energy Park, Tissue Culture Park and Agri Park (all Jalgaon, Maharashtra), JISL Kondamadgu (Hyderabad, Telangana), JISL Udumalpeth (Tamil Nadu), JISL Alwar (Rajasthan), and Jain Farm Fresh Foods plants at Jalgaon (Maharashtra), Chittoor Unit-1 and Unit-2 (Andhra Pradesh) and Vadodara (Gujarat)
- GHG footprint reported and assured under the BRSR Core: Gross Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions (tCO2e), with emissions intensity per unit of revenue from operations (PPP adjusted) and per unit of product/output, quantified using GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard methodologies
- Water footprint reported: total water consumption, water consumption intensity per unit of revenue (PPP adjusted) and per unit of product/output, and water discharged by destination and level of treatment
- Energy footprint reported: total energy consumed in GJ, percentage of renewable energy consumed, and energy intensity on both revenue and production bases
- Circularity/waste management reported by category (plastic, e-waste, bio-medical, construction and demolition, battery, other hazardous and non-hazardous), with total waste generated, waste intensity, waste recovered through recycling/re-use and waste disposed by method; radioactive waste is reported as not applicable
- Employee well-being and safety KPIs assured: spending on employee and worker well-being as a % of total revenue, safety incidents for employees and contract workforce, permanent disabilities, Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) and fatalities
- Gender diversity and equal opportunity KPIs assured: gross wages paid to females as a % of wages paid, and POSH complaints reported, as a % of female employees/workers, and upheld
- Inclusive development KPIs assured: input material sourced directly from MSMEs/small producers and from within India as a % of total purchases, and wages paid to persons employed in smaller towns as a % of total wage cost
- Fairness and openness KPIs assured: data breach instances as a % of cyber security events, days of accounts payable, concentration of purchases and sales with trading houses, dealers and related parties, and share of related-party transactions in purchases, sales, loans and advances and investments
- Reporting against GRI Standards 2021 topic standards - Energy (302), Water and Effluents (303), Emissions (305), Waste (306), Employment (401), Occupational Health and Safety (403), Training and Education (404), Diversity and Equal Opportunity (405), Local Communities (413), Supplier Social Assessment (414), Public Policy (415) and Customer Health and Safety (416)
- Business-model ESG linkage: the Company promotes climate-smart agricultural technologies, precision irrigation systems, efficient water management solutions and sustainable farming practices as its stated response to climate and water-resource pressure, and emphasises quality, traceability, food safety and sustainable sourcing in the food business
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The main capacity addition disclosed for FY2026 was in the Agro-Food Processing business run through Jain Farm Fresh Foods Limited (JFFFL), where the Company successfully commissioned two high-speed bottling lines for juices and carbonated soft drinks for one of India's leading beverage companies, resulting in a significant expansion of its private label and contract manufacturing business; management states the commissioning of these new beverage bottling facilities further strengthened manufacturing capabilities and expanded the Company's presence in the growing private label and contract manufacturing segment. JFFFL's footprint spans manufacturing facilities and business operations across India, Turkey, Belgium, the United Kingdom and the United States, serving food manufacturers, food service companies, institutional buyers, retail chains, private label brands and co-manufacturing partners. Going forward the Company says continued investments in innovation, manufacturing capabilities, private label solutions and operational excellence are expected to further strengthen its competitive position, and it remains committed to enhancing productivity across the value chain and improving processing efficiencies. In plastics, expansion is described qualitatively rather than as projects: in PVC Sheets/WPC the Company intends to strengthen its presence by introducing value-added products, expanding market reach and enhancing customer engagement on the back of established manufacturing capabilities and an expanding distribution network. Management also flags capacity utilisation risk - utilisation across businesses may be influenced by seasonal demand, Government programme implementation, customer demand patterns and market conditions - and says it continues to improve utilisation through product diversification, expansion of the retail business, export growth, introduction of value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations. No rupee capex outlay, dated project pipeline or plant-wise capacity table is disclosed in this section.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government focus on rural drinking water through the Jal Jeevan Mission, plus PMAY, AMRUT, Swachh Bharat Mission, PMKSY and irrigation expansion, is expected to provide sustained demand for plastic piping
- Stabilisation of PVC resin prices and gradual normalisation of channel inventories, together with improving demand from agriculture, housing and infrastructure, are expected to support recovery in the domestic plastic piping business
- Increasing replacement demand, growing awareness of BIS-certified products and rising adoption of modern plumbing systems are expected to provide further growth opportunities
- HDPE adoption driven by water supply investment, irrigation, city gas distribution network expansion, wastewater treatment and industrial infrastructure; superior strength, flexibility, corrosion resistance and long service life support substitution away from steel and concrete
- PVC Sheets and Wood Polymer Composite demand supported by urbanisation, residential and commercial construction and a shift toward lightweight, durable, moisture-resistant and recyclable building materials replacing wood, plywood and metal
- Agro-Food Processing outlook supported by changing consumer preferences, demand for processed and convenience foods, focus on food safety and traceability, expansion of organised retail and food service, and India's position as a large producer of fruits, vegetables and spices with cost-competitive manufacturing
- Hi-Tech Agri was the growth engine, with segment margins over 18% described as among the best in precision agriculture globally, and the shift towards retail, exports, value-added products and cash-and-carry business gathering pace
- Tissue culture demand demonstrated by a single day's dispatch of 1,253,191 banana plantlets; the innovation pipeline includes new variety introductions Jain Sweet Orange-6 and Jain Mandarin-1
- Dehydrated Ingredients Division recorded one of its best years in three decades; the fruit business held volumes and profitability even as softer farm-gate prices lowered reported realisations
- Overseas plastics: Ex-cel Plastics held a strong position in European PVC foam sheets, UK and Ireland operations served building products, packaging, storage systems and technical plastics, and the addition of Harlequin extended reach into wastewater treatment, rainwater harvesting and storage
- Headwind: unseasonal rainfall affected crops and demand in several markets, and the domestic piping business bore the brunt of PVC resin price swings, cautious dealer stocking and slower infrastructure execution
- Watch-item: the IMD forecast the southwest monsoon at 90% of the Long Period Average, signalling early stress for India's farm economy and raising food-security concerns
- Watch-item: continuing global conflicts and looming disruptions to supply chains and logistics put pressure on day-to-day working of the Company
- Received a ₹135 crore order for 5,438 solar agricultural pumps under Maharashtra's solar pump programme, following successful execution of the earlier phase
- Completed subsea execution of India's largest single HDPE marine intake pipeline for the Perur site of Chennai's 400 MLD desalination plant, adding to a portfolio that already includes the Minjur desalination plant
- Commissioned and inaugurated the Gendoli-Folai Lift Irrigation Project in Rajasthan, which will irrigate around 4,000 hectares and benefit close to 25,000 farmers across 17 villages using solar power

The Company will invest in climate-smart irrigation, biotechnology, disease-resilient planting material, protected cultivation, digital farming, solar energy, food technology and circular agricultural systems.
Management flagged that continuing conflicts around the world and looming disruptions to global supply chains and logistics put real pressure on the day-to-day working of the Company.

The Company will continue to invest in innovation, manufacturing capabilities, private label solutions and operational excellence, and to enhance productivity across the value chain, improve processing efficiencies and expand value-added product offerings in Agro-Food Processing.

The Company continues to improve capacity utilisation across its businesses through product diversification, expansion of the retail business, export growth, introduction of value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations.
In the PVC Sheets and WPC business the Company will continue to strengthen its presence by introducing value-added products, expanding market reach and enhancing customer engagement.

risks.note: The Company's businesses remain exposed to fluctuations in prices of key raw materials, particularly plastic resins and certain agricultural commodities. Since effective hedging mechanisms for plastic resins are not available, it can only monitor market movements and adjust procurement, pricing and inventory strategies; PVC resin swings during FY2026 drove channel inventory rationalisation and cautious dealer procurement.
risks.risk: Raw material price risk - exposure to plastic resin and agricultural commodity prices with no effective hedge

risks.note: Liquidity management is explicitly listed among corporate-level risks. The Company relies on a disciplined approach to operating cash flow and working capital efficiency - retail-led model, cash-and-carry sales, improved collections, inventory optimisation and prudent capital allocation - and reports that it continued to meet all debt servicing obligations and maintained its borrowings as 'Standard' with all lending institutions.

Timely recovery of receivables, particularly under Government-supported programmes, remains an important focus area. Mitigation is a deliberate shift towards the retail-led business model and cash-and-carry sales while reducing dependence on project-based business, backed by dealer relationships and disciplined credit management.
risks.risk: Receivables and collection risk, especially under Government-supported programmes

risks.note: Changing climatic conditions, erratic rainfall patterns, extreme weather events and increasing pressure on water resources continue to impact agricultural activity and demand across the Company's businesses - the same forces that also create demand for its climate-smart irrigation and water-management solutions.

Demand across businesses is influenced by agricultural activity, Government policies, infrastructure spending, rural income levels and overall economic conditions, making the order profile dependent on programme implementation; the Company leans on its MIS, extensive dealer network and market intelligence to track requirements.
risks.risk: Demand risk tied to agricultural activity, Government policy and infrastructure spending

risks.note: Geopolitical developments, changing international trade policies, reciprocal tariff measures, supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures and global economic uncertainty may impact both domestic and international operations; diversification and global presence are the stated mitigants.

Domestic and international operations expose the Company to interest rate and currency movements; it uses treasury management practices including forward exchange contracts where considered necessary, alongside a continued focus on cash flows and working capital.
risks.risk: Interest rate and foreign exchange risk

risks.note: Utilisation across businesses may be influenced by seasonal demand, Government programme implementation, customer demand patterns and overall market conditions; the Company works to improve it through product diversification, retail expansion, export growth, value-added products and optimisation of manufacturing operations.
